texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are that on 15.05.2018 on receipt of DD no. 12A, SI Rajkumar reached Flyover of Kotla Mubarakpur where he found a motorcycle no. DL-3SDY-4577 in accidental condition and a car no. DL-9CAN-0404(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle). On receipt of information, IO reached AIIMS Trauma Center where he met the victim/injured Gopi Singh and Chetan. Injured Gopi Singh stated that he was going to his house on his bike with his friend, from AIIMS hospital. When he reached at Andrewsganj Flyover, he drove his motorbike on traffic light turning green. At that time, the offending vehicle came from the left side and hit the motorcycle due to which petitioner Gopi Singh received grievous injury on his leg while his friend received simple injury on his left thumb. He stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. 3. An FIR no.154 of 2018 dated 15.05.2018 was registered u/s 279,337,338 of IPC at PS Kotla Mubarakpur and the matter was investigated. After investigation a charge sheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle(Respondent no.1) while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Respondent no.1 is driver of offending vehicle, Respondent no.2 is owner of offending vehicle and Respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the DAR, written statement/reply was filed by Respondent no.3 pleading that accident took place due to sole carelessness and negligence of the claimants. Involvement of offending vehicle is denied. However, insurance of the offending vehicle is admitted on the date of accident. No reply/written statement was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2 despite opportunity. 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 20.03.2019. OPP. 3. Relief. Gopi Singh (Dar) vs Ritesh Kumar (154/18 K.M. Pur) on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128836295/ 2 7. Thereafter, petitioner Gopi Singh examined himself as PW-1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. As per the affidavit, on 15.05.2018 at about 11 AM, petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SDY-4577 and was going to his home from AIIMS alongwith pillion rider Chetan. When he reached under Flyover, Andrews Ganj, suddenly a car i.e. offending vehicle bearing no.DL-9CAN-0404 which was being driven rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle of the injured. CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.10 17:03:15 +0530 MACT NO: 912/18 Gopi Singh v. Ritesh Kumar P.No. 3 Of 18 BK Due to such impact he alongwith pillion rider fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries in his left foot and all over his body. He was taken to JPN Apex Trauma Center where doctor declared his injuries as grievous. Thereafter, he was admitted at Holy Family Hospital where he was operated and was under observation for about 6 months. He deposed that he had spent Rs.2 lac on his treatment, special diet and conveyance etc. He was 19 years old at the time of accident and his date of birth is 04.12.1999. He was working as Delivery boy with Swiggy at Malviya Nagar, New Delhi and was getting salary of Rs.16,000/- p.m. Due to said accident , he was unable to do work for about 6 months and even was unable to do his daily routine work. He relied upon Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, his driving licence as Ex.PW-1/2, 10th school certificate as Ex.PW-1/3, MLC as Ex.PW-1/4, Discharge summary /OPD cards as Ex.PW- 1/5(colly), Medical bills as Ex.PW-1/6 and DAR as Ex.PW- 1/7(colly). PW-1 was duly examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company and Respondent no.1 and 2. No other evidence was led by petitioner. Respondents did not lead any evidence. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimants and the Respondents. Gopi Singh (Dar) vs Ritesh Kumar (154/18 K.M. Pur) on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128836295/ 3 10. In the instant case, petitioner no.2/injured/pillion rider Chetan settled his claim with the respondents and thus no observation qua his claim is being passed. Petitioner no.1/Gopi Singh has asserted that the accident occurred on 15.05.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by Respondent no.1. He denied the suggestion of negligence on his part or the allegation that he had jumped the red light. He denied the suggestion that he was not wearing helmet. He admitted that he did not suffer any permanent disability. He denied the suggestion that the injuries suffered by him have not been caused by Respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle. Petitioner has sustained a rigorous cross-examination and nothing material to discredit him, could be brought on record despite the cross-examination. Further, after investigating even the police has filed a chargesheet against Respondent no.1. P.No. 5 Of 18 BK was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle . 11. Only suggestions denying rash & negligence of Respondent no.1 were put to PW-1 during cross-examination. To rebut the claim of the petitioner they have not led any evidence in their defence. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
